records.description: The triggered optical coincidence summary and response-conditioned anticorrelation support nonclassical counting in one named preparation. Capture-photon wavelength and the corrected meson radiative ratio separately constrain their declared emission observables. This comparison preserves formal photon-state conventions, detector response and dependent analysis stages instead of treating them as one universal photon-property measurement.
records.name: Scoped photon evidence comparison
openObligations: The optical count summary and its inferred alpha statistic reuse the same acquisition. Their two study records distinguish measurement from interpretation, not independent replications. The same-source Mach-Zehnder visibility uses a changed configuration and cannot demonstrate simultaneous which-path information, a permanent trajectory or independent source confirmation.

The printed Grangier selected point lacks the transmitted singles rate, complete event stream, efficiency calibration and full likelihood. Its alpha uncertainty and greater-than-13-standard-deviation comparison remain publication reports, not an exact replay, trial-corrected significance or a general exclusion of all classical detector models.

The capture wavelength retains the 1999 crystal calibration and the explicitly identified later calibration/adjustment limits. The corrected KLOE radiative branching-ratio ratio retains its efficiency, daughter-branch, interference and statistical/systematic assumptions; it is not an absolute decay width or the conditional pseudoscalar mixing angle.

Optical coincidences, gamma-ray diffraction wavelength and a corrected meson decay ratio have different preparations, response models, units and inference stages. They are not one pooled photon-count sample or joint significance test. No new acquisition, independent raw-data fit, model discrimination beyond the declared counting assumptions or complete QED-to-macroscopic-light chain is claimed.

The measurements do not establish exactly zero photon mass or charge, distinguishable persistent identity, a static Coulomb photon flux, atomic binding, an oriented vacuum or universal photon-driven biological organization. These boundaries remain those of the formal scope definition.

contexts.finding: At the selected low-excitation setting, the paper reports 9 joint-output coincidences in approximately 5 hours. The gate rate N_1 is approximately 8800 s^-1, including a 300 s^-1 dark rate; the reflected singles rate N_r is approximately 5 s^-1 with dark rate 0.02 s^-1. N_t, N_r and N_c denote gated transmitted singles, reflected singles and coincidences, and the observed probabilities are p_t=N_t/N_1, p_r=N_r/N_1 and p_c=N_c/N_1.
limitations: Partial printed rates and exposure do not provide a complete event stream, full source-state characterization or independent detector calibration.

The named article refers source construction to an earlier paper. Atomic species, transition wavelengths, collection geometry in full detail and a complete state tomography are not supplied here. The authors explicitly distinguish their preparation from an ideal shuttered, fully collected single-photon source.
Multiple cascades, finite collection, detector inefficiency and dark triggers remain possible. A herald does not guarantee that an emitted nu_2 photon reaches or is detected at either output.

These are printed selected-point summaries, not a complete event table. The selected transmitted rate N_t, exact exposure, joint calibration and event stream are absent, so alpha and its uncertainty cannot be exactly reconstructed locally from these rounded values.

The reported dark-rate inclusions do not specify an exhaustive background-subtraction procedure. Nine detections do not imply ideal zero coincidences, unit efficiency or a measured particle trajectory.
contexts.observable: Herald gates, transmitted/reflected singles and joint-output coincidence counts
contexts.preparation: A two-photon-excited radiative cascade emits distinct frequencies nu_1 and nu_2. Detecting nu_1 triggers a gate for photomultipliers at the transmitted and reflected nu_2 outputs of a beam splitter. The intermediate lifetime is 4.7 ns; the selected gate is approximately 9 ns. The counters register gates, each output and joint output detections. This is a conditional detection preparation, not an ideal deterministic source in a single spatial mode.

contexts.finding: The selected experiment reports alpha=0.18 +/- 0.06, below the stated semiclassical bound 1; Figure 2 error bars denote one standard deviation. For that setting the publication gives a classical expected coincidence count of at least 50 versus the 9 observed and reports a separation exceeding 13 standard deviations. A pulsed-diode control matched trigger and singles probabilities and satisfied the classical inequality. This supports nonclassical optical counting within the declared response assumptions.
limitations: The same source, acquisition and gate selection underlie both study records. No independent replication, exact statistical replay or proof of all photon properties is supplied.

The classical bound is conditional on this common-intensity, fixed-response photodetection model, including the factorized conditional output response in its coincidence formula. It does not exclude every imaginable classical detector model. Saturated, nonlinear or spuriously correlated detector responses require separate validation.

N is the cascade-excitation rate, not the trigger rate N_1; the model relates them by N_1=epsilon_1*N. No exact f(w), source intensity, all efficiencies or full likelihood are reconstructed. The published comparison uses the same counted data, not an independent experiment.

The error distance is source-reported, not an independently recomputed Gaussian tail, exact small-count likelihood, trial-corrected significance or proof of zero systematic error. Rounded 9-versus-at-least-50 counts do not reproduce the full comparison or an uncertainty model.

Using the same source and trigger, a separately configured Mach-Zehnder experiment gave gated fringe visibility above 98 percent, with a dark-count correction below 0.3 percent. The 98.7 +/- 0.5 percent value is its ungated calibration. The arrangements are mutually exclusive; their shared source is not independent replication or a simultaneous which-path/interference measurement.

The result is compatible with a near-single-photon preparation, not proof of a literal unsplit trajectory, a deterministic photon source, electromagnetic-field quantization in every regime, all photon properties or a complete QED-to-macroscopic-light chain.

records.description: In the specified free Maxwell theory, fix an inertial frame, hbar=c=1 and nonzero momentum p. Locally choose a real transverse basis E(p)=(epsilon_1,epsilon_2), with E^T E=I and p^T E=0. For the existing one-photon wavepacket use dPi_p=d^3p/(2pi)^3 and f_r(p)=g(p)c_r(p), where c_dagger c=1 on the nonzero support of g, integral dPi_p |g|^2=1 and integral dPi_p |p| |g|^2 is finite. Its complex polarization vector is e(p)=E(p)c(p), so p dot e=0 and e_dagger e=1. Here e is a polarization amplitude, not the mean electric field, which vanishes in this one-photon number state. A passive real O(p) in SO(2) gives E'=E O, c'=O^T c and f'=O^T f in the transformed mode convention; transforming creation operators consistently preserves e and the one-photon state. An active polarization comparison instead fixes the basis and apparatus while varying relative coefficients. Both transverse modes have the same free frequency |p|; this model supplies no polarization-dependent propagation splitting or preferred vacuum axis.

rationale.statement: In the specified free Maxwell theory, fix an inertial frame, hbar=c=1 and nonzero momentum p. Locally choose a real transverse basis E(p)=(epsilon_1,epsilon_2), with E^T E=I and p^T E=0. For the existing one-photon wavepacket use dPi_p=d^3p/(2pi)^3 and f_r(p)=g(p)c_r(p), where c_dagger c=1 on the nonzero support of g, integral dPi_p |g|^2=1 and integral dPi_p |p| |g|^2 is finite. Its complex polarization vector is e(p)=E(p)c(p), so p dot e=0 and e_dagger e=1. Here e is a polarization amplitude, not the mean electric field, which vanishes in this one-photon number state. An active polarization comparison instead fixes the basis and apparatus while varying relative coefficients. Both transverse modes have the same free frequency |p|; this model supplies no polarization-dependent propagation splitting or preferred vacuum axis.

The high-multipole union is TT 30-2508 and TE/EE 30-1996, with narrower pair-specific cuts. These response-conditioned angular correlations are distinct from a primordial curvature spectrum or an observed quantum-vacuum realization.

openObligations: The actual Plik data vector keeps frequency-pair spectra; it is not the frequency-coadded curve in Figures 57-59. Those displays fix foreground/nuisance parameters to a best fit including lensing reconstruction, and their high-multipole diagonal error bars omit foreground-model uncertainty. limitations: Not all corrections are freely fitted: the baseline fixes EE dust amplitudes, polarization-efficiency corrections and several residual templates, while fitting selected foreground/calibration parameters with priors. Shared scanning systematics can remain correlated between half missions.

Simulations and fiducial covariance approximate noise, foregrounds, sample variance and residual systematics. The source reports finite-simulation and fixed-sky limitations; validation is not proof that all calibration, foreground or likelihood errors vanish. No maps, templates, covariance or end-to-end simulation are locally reconstructed.

contexts.observable: Response-conditioned angular spectra and their joint statistical/nuisance treatment
contexts.preparation: Commander jointly models low-temperature foregrounds and the CMB. SimAll uses foreground-cleaned 100 x 143 GHz quasi-QML polarization estimates and simulation-based probabilities. High-multipole Plik uses masked, beam-corrected half-mission cross-spectra with noise/covariance models and foreground, calibration, polarization-efficiency and temperature-to-polarization leakage treatment. Its covariance retains correlations between frequency pairs and TT, TE and EE using a fiducial model. Cross-spectra reduce additive noise bias only insofar as the split-map noises are uncorrelated.
